In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
topsoil removal (erosion) and one-time manure applications are detrimental to the soil system, and that the legacy effect of the manure application can be observed for at least 22 years.

topsoil removal to a depth of 20 cm, superimposed with one-time manure applications, had a significant impact on soil quality attributes, but not on soil resilience, and that the legacy effect of one-time manures application was still evident in 2012.

topsoil erosion (cuts) and one-time organic amendments (manure) had significant and long-lasting effects on soil quality attributes and soil resilience, but the legacy effect of manures was more persistent and pronounced than that of topsoil erosion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
topsoil removal (cutting) and one-time amendments (manure and fertilizer) have long-term legacy effects on soil quality, but the effects are not additive.
topsoil removal (cuts) had no lasting effect on C and N fractions and soil aggregation if organic amendments were not applied.
topsoil removal (cuts) and one-time organic amendments have long-term impacts on soil quality and resilience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of disturbance on soil quality attributes are short-lived and can be mitigated with organic amendment application.
topsoil removal can have a long-lasting effect on soil quality and that one-time application of organic amendments (e.g., manure) can provide a long-lasting legacy effect.
soil quality can recover from topsoil loss and that manure can be a valuable soil amendment for improving soil quality and soil resilience.
